claim_boundary: Primary evidence is mixed: older high-frequency Bitcoin studies report statistically significant serial dependence at 1H, while newer robust inference reports returns broadly uncorrelated over time. Neither result establishes a profitable DRA entry filter. Exactly one separately frozen equal-capital historical screen may test whether a relatively high prior-day H1 lag-1 return autocorrelation percentile distinguishes less oscillatory or more persistent DRA momentum entries; failure closes this exact family without tuning.

feature_contract.formula: Pearson correlation of the 23 ordered adjacent pairs formed from exactly 24 open-to-close H1 log returns wholly inside the latest complete UTC day, midranked against exactly the prior 20 complete-day coefficients

prior_matrix.finding: The authors report statistically significant lower-order autocorrelation on 5-minute and 1-hour cryptocurrency returns, with BTC 1H lower-order autocorrelation negative in their sample; they explicitly state that inefficiency alone is insufficient to extract profits.
prior_matrix.identity: Tartakovsky, Plesovskikh, Sarmakeeva and Bibik, Autocorrelation of returns in major cryptocurrency markets (2020)
prior_matrix.transfer_boundary: Bitfinex and BitMEX evidence through 2019 does not establish OKX H1 persistence, a one-day coefficient, a rolling percentile, DRA timing or strategy economics.

prior_matrix.finding: Variance-ratio tests at 15-, 30-, 60- and 120-minute frequencies reject memoryless Bitcoin returns in the study's historical sample.
prior_matrix.identity: Zargar and Kumar, Informational inefficiency of Bitcoin: A study based on high-frequency data (2019)
prior_matrix.transfer_boundary: A martingale rejection is not a directional trading rule and supplies no DRA threshold, cost model or matched-capital evidence.

prior_matrix.finding: Using robust inference designed for heavy tails and nonlinear dependence, the authors report that Bitcoin and Ethereum returns are broadly uncorrelated over time despite volatility clustering.
prior_matrix.identity: Abdullaev and Ibragimov, Stylized facts of cryptocurrency markets: Robust definitions and inference approaches (2026)
prior_matrix.transfer_boundary: Aggregate uncorrelatedness does not rule out conditional entry-selection value, but it makes persistence of the older H1 effect uncertain and requires direct economic falsification.

real_time_design_requirements: Use exactly 24 open-to-close H1 log returns wholly contained in the latest complete UTC day; never include a preceding-day close or later bar.
Compute Pearson lag-1 correlation from 23 ordered adjacent pairs with separately demeaned leading and lagged sequences; fail closed if either sequence has zero variation.
Convert only the latest complete-day coefficient to a midrank percentile against exactly the prior 20 complete-day coefficients.
Keep DRA parent side, entries, exits, lot cost, capacity, fee, adverse slippage, cooldown and next-bar fill clock unchanged.
Freeze primary 0.5 and neighbors 0.4 and 0.6 before outcome access; do not search another percentile, lookback, return definition, lag, correlation estimator or relation.

Require Design and Validation total and realized PnL improvement, annual breadth, drawdown and underwater non-inferiority, holding support, terminal inventory and neighbor stability under gate set V2; otherwise close the family.
Do not open post-2024 OOS or create a candidate from this prior audit.
uncertainty: A coefficient estimated from 23 adjacent pairs is noisy and may be dominated by a small number of hourly moves.
Older BTC evidence often found negative rather than positive 1H autocorrelation, while newer robust evidence finds no aggregate linear autocorrelation.
The within-day percentile and DRA admission transfer are preregistered research choices, not strategies reported by the cited papers.
No post-2024 evidence, OOS, candidate, runtime filter or Trading path was accessed or authorized.
